title: GPTScan: Detecting Logic Vulnerabilities in Smart Contracts by Combining GPT with Program Analysis

key_numbers.metric: Static confirmation filters false-positive candidate functions

structure_gain: Static (dataflow) confirmation of GPT-recognized key variables/statements filters 65.84% of false-positive candidates on the same GPT-3.5-turbo pipeline (647->221 functions, Sec 5.3 Table 4) — a same-model component ablation isolating the symbolic stage, consistent with the corpus's RepoAudit-style neuro-symbolic isolation coding.
confound_note: RQ3 ablation holds model (GPT-3.5-turbo), prompts, and candidate set constant and varies only the presence of static confirmation — component-isolated; cross-dataset precision differences (90.91% vs 57.14%) reflect dataset difficulty, not the ablation.
stop_detail: Logic-vulnerability types are decomposed into scenario+property sentences matched by GPT against statically pre-filtered candidate functions; GPT then names key variables/statements, which static dataflow confirmation validates before a finding is reported (Secs 4.2-4.4); cost 14.39 s / $0.01 per KLoC (Sec 5.4, Table 5).
threats_to_datum: Record restored after a screening-to-extraction handoff loss (screened include in decisions_chunk1 under its OpenAlex/DOI identity, which carried no arxiv_id; documented in decisions_adjudication.json D2). Author-extracted and author-verified directly against arxiv.org/html/2308.03314 (2026-08-30); not covered by the blind second coding (corpus coverage 67/68), disclosed in Appendix B.

stop_detail: The lightweight Explorer agent uses read-only repo tools (ls, glob, grep, read_file) to gather Repository Context, Code Evidence, and Security Findings on demand, reporting back to the Planning agent, which forms and refines vulnerability hypotheses (Planner-Explorer architecture section).
threats_to_datum: RepoPairBench is small (100 vulnerability-fix pairs / 200 instances) and Python-only, with C/C++ extension left as future work; the pair-correctness metric requires both vulnerable and fixed versions to be classified correctly, a stricter and less standard metric than typical F1/precision, complicating cross-paper comparison.
title: DREA: Decoupled Reasoning and Exploration Agents for Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection

datasets: 450 NFT contract samples (custom, from real NFT projects / public vulnerability datasets)
structure_gain: +13.33pp / +10.0pp deltas correct, but same-model/config constancy is not substantiated (settings 'not recorded') and complete-contract inputs are far longer than slices — unequal context budget.
confound_note: The three-arm ablation (slice+knowledge / slice-knowledge / full-contract-knowledge) holds the LLM (DeepSeek) fixed and cleanly varies representation and knowledge-injection, but the outcome metric is a raw 'positive label rate' with no independent ground truth, so the delta may partly reflect a shift toward over-flagging rather than true detection accuracy.
stop_detail: A structure-aware context-window algorithm regex-locates candidate statements, expands to a syntactically balanced function-scoped slice, and embeds an ERC-721-specific knowledge base plus a closed label set and explicit 'return None if insufficient evidence' rejection rule directly in the prompt (Section 4.2-4.3, Algorithm 1, Prompt 1).
threats_to_datum: Authors explicitly warn the positive-label rate 'must not be interpreted as classification accuracy' since there is no independently annotated ground truth, confusion matrix, or per-class precision/recall; model ID, temperature, and full knowledge-base content are unrecorded, limiting reproducibility (Section 6).
title: Ethereum NFT Smart Contracts: Knowledge-Guided Vulnerability Detection with LLM and Code Slicing

structure_gain: Full CLEAR (with Vulnerability Causal Knowledge Graph context) vs. No-VCKG ablation, same multi-agent LLM pipeline, on PrimeVul: Pairwise-Correct 19.17 vs. 8.08 (Table 3); removing only Fix-Intent nodes drops it to 14.32 vs. 19.17 full.
confound_note: Table 3's node-ablation removes individual VCKG node types (or the whole VCKG) while holding the multi-agent (Collector/Claim/Critic/Judge) architecture and base LLM fixed, isolating the causal-context representation's contribution; the headline 130.7%/71.56% figures instead compare CLEAR's full pipeline against a different prior system (VulTrial), which is not representation-isolated.
stop_detail: Grounded via a Vulnerability Causal Knowledge Graph built offline from CVE descriptions, patches, and source code (LLM-extracted causal chains linked by semantic-similarity neighborhood edges and cross-instance global edges); a Collector Agent retrieves the Top-5 similar historical Entrypoints and traverses Local/Neighbor/Global edges, serializing the result into the Claim/Critic/Judge agents' prompts (VCKG construction / Collector Agent section).
threats_to_datum: Authors note semantic similarity used to build VCKG edges does not guarantee causal consistency (nodes can be linked despite being causally unrelated, or left disconnected despite sharing a mechanism); human inter-rater agreement on Global Edge validity is only moderate (kappa=0.51); causal claims are LLM-derived, not symbolically verified.
title: CLEAR: Causal Context-Based Agentic Reasoning for Vulnerability Detection

venue: Georgia Institute of Technology Master's practicum project (not peer-reviewed)
demote_reason: Full text confirms the entire pipeline targets securing AI-generated code itself: Python code is generated from LLMSecEval prompts by a Code Generation LLM, vulnerabilities are found by CodeQL/Bandit static analyzers (not by an LLM-based representation/context mechanism as the analysis technique), and the LLM's role is generation and remediation of its own output, enriched with MITRE ATT&CK/CWE context. This is security of LLM-generated code, not use of program representations/context to drive LLM-based security analysis of arbitrary code (E4).
title: Securing AI-Generated Code: A Just-in-Time Vulnerability Detection and Remediation Pipeline
